title: Kiln session record
description: Which Pi session is this project's planning conversation. ⚠️ IT EXISTS SO A RESUME CANNOT ATTACH TO A STRANGER. Pi sessions are just files in a directory; without a record naming the one Kiln started, 'resume the session' means 'resume the most recent one', which on a shared session directory is somebody else's conversation. ⚠️ MISSING OR CORRUPT IS A RECOVERABLE STATE, NOT A FATAL ONE (section 12): present the available Kiln sessions or start a new one — never silently resume an unrelated generic Pi session. ⚠️ IT STORES A MODE AND NOT A PATH. The external state root is derived from the project id, so writing the resolved directory here would put an absolute user path into a file, which REQ-0024 forbids and which would break the moment the same project was opened on another machine.

projectId.description: ⚠️ CARRIED SO THE RECORD CAN BE DISOWNED. Local state can outlive the project it belonged to — a directory reused, a project re-initialised — and a session record whose project id does not match `.pi/kiln.json` belongs to something else and must not be resumed.

sessionId.description: Pi's own identifier for the session. Opaque here on purpose: its shape belongs to Pi and pinning a format would be Kiln asserting something about a file it does not own.

stateMode.description: Which state policy was in force when this session was recorded — project-local ignored state, or the external per-user root. ⚠️ RECORDED BECAUSE IT DECIDES WHERE TO LOOK. A record written under one mode and read under the other would send the resume at a directory that does not hold the session, and the honest outcome is to notice rather than to search both.

lastResumedAt.description: ⚠️ FOR A HUMAN CHOOSING BETWEEN SESSIONS, not for the machine choosing one. Recovery presents the available sessions; it does not pick the newest, because 'most recent' is the heuristic this record exists to replace.
